plain_english_policy: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to allow Franklin County's governing body (the Commission) the authority to redirect one-fourth of its existing sales tax revenue. Currently, this portion of the tax is designated for public schools under Section 40-12-4 of the Code of Alabama. The new rule would permit the county to use these funds specifically as matching money for grants from the state's 'Alabama Transportation Rehabilitation and Improvement Program' (roads). This authority is set to last for two years starting October 1, 2014, but can be renewed in subsequent two-year periods only if Franklin County voters approve it via a referendum.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would produce a policy shift allowing local government officials in Franklin County flexibility to prioritize road infrastructure projects over school funding for the first year of implementation (two years), provided they secure state grants. The change is not permanent; it requires ongoing voter approval every two years to continue.
evidence_quotes: "Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 40-12-4... may allocate one-fourth of the proceeds of the one cent tax levied in Franklin County... for the purpose of matching funds for any grant from the Alabama Transportation Rehabilitation and Improvement Program."
"The authority granted by this amendment is effective for two years.""The authority may be extended from time to time for subsequent two-year periods if approved by a majority vote of the voters"
